Source: wash2/accesskit cosmic-0.14, commit f0599eed5f18111228266fe3f28991cc48b5964f.

Local patch adds AT-SPI EditableText to writable text controls explicitly supporting string SetValue. The supported method is SetTextContents, dispatched as Action::SetValue with string data. InsertText, DeleteText, clipboard and attribute editing explicitly return false; this patch does not claim those operations are implemented. The existing Text interface continues to provide caret and selection operations when the control advertises SetTextSelection.

Local patch also keeps the adapter context alive when the D-Bus session bus or the AT-SPI bus is unreachable. Upstream unwraps the event loop's result, so a refused AT-SPI connection panics the context thread and disables accessibility for the rest of the process, and a missing session bus ends the thread without retrying. The context now keeps its adapters and message receiver across outages: adapters are deactivated while no AT-SPI bus is connected and asked for a fresh initial tree once one is. Failed and lost connections, detected through zbus `Connection::closed` or an adapter-message error, are retried after 1 second, doubling to at most 30 seconds; the session and AT-SPI buses back off independently. The first failure of an outage is a `tracing` warning and later attempts are debug messages. An outage ends only once a connection stays up for 30 seconds, so a bus that accepts and then drops connections keeps backing off. An unreadable screen-reader status counts as disabled. The context also watches the owner of `org.a11y.Bus`, so a launcher that starts late, leaves or restarts is followed without polling. Retries stop while the screen reader is disabled, and the context returns once every message sender is dropped. The `async-io` feature waits with `async_io::Timer`; `futures-util` is no longer used. The tests re-execute the test binary per scenario with private `dbus-daemon` buses, so they need `dbus-daemon` and never contact the user's buses. Remove this part when upstream recovers from unreachable buses equivalently.

The two crate manifests are standalone copies of the pinned workspace manifests; the common/consumer types stay at the exact same Git tag and lock revision. The accesskit-unix manifest adds `tracing` and, for `async-io`, `async-io`; both are already in the dependency graph. Upstream license files are retained. Remove the EditableText part when the pinned Linux adapter provides equivalent string replacement. No ABI or wire protocol change is introduced.
